        "contents": "  v_identity jsonb;\nbegin\n  -- Check if this is a Google OAuth user by examining identities\n  -- Google OAuth users will have an identity with provider = 'google'\n  if new.identities is not null then\n    for v_identity in \n      select value from jsonb_array_elements(new.identities)\n    loop\n      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then\n        v_is_google_user := true;\n        exit;\n      end if;\n    end loop;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Only proceed if this is a Google OAuth user\n  if not v_is_google_user then\n    return new;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Extract Google email (primary email from auth.users)\n  v_google_email := new.email;\n\n  -- Extract Google full name from raw_user_meta_data\n  -- Try multiple possible keys: full_name, name\n  v_google_full_name := coalesce(\n    new.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'full_name',\n    new.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'name'\n  );\n\n  -- Extract Google profile picture from raw_user_meta_data\n  -- Try multiple possible keys: avatar_url, picture\n  v_google_profile_picture := coalesce(\n    new.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'avatar_url',\n    new.raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'picture'\n  );\n\n  -- Insert into public.users table with all extracted Google data\n  -- Use ON CONFLICT to handle race conditions (if record already exists, update it)\n  insert into public.users (\n    auth_user_id,\n    google_email,\n    google_full_name,\n    google_profile_picture\n  )\n  values (\n    new.id,\n    v_google_email,\n    v_google_full_name,\n    v_google_profile_picture\n  )\n  on conflict (auth_user_id) do update\n  set\n    google_email = excluded.google_email,\n    google_full_name = excluded.google_full_name,\n    google_profile_picture = excluded.google_profile_picture,\n    updated_at = now();\n\n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_new_google_user() is 'Trigger function that automatically populates public.users table when a Google OAuth user is created in auth.users.         "contents": "-- Enable realtime publication for users table\nalter publication supabase_realtime add table public.users;\n\n-- Create trigger function for realtime broadcasting on users table\n-- Uses realtime.broadcast_changes for database change notifications\ncreate or replace function public.users_realtime_broadcast_trigger()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Broadcast changes to users table using dedicated topic pattern\n  -- Topic format: users:{user_id} for user-specific updates\n  perform realtime.broadcast_changes(\n    tg_table_name || ':' || coalesce(new.id, old.id)::text,\n    tg_op,\n    tg_op,\n    tg_table_name,\n    tg_table_schema,\n    new,\n    old\n  );\n  return coalesce(new, old);\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.users_realtime_broadcast_trigger() is 'Trigger function that broadcasts changes to the users table via Supabase Realtime.         "contents": "-- Migration: Restrict signups to Google OAuth only\n-- Purpose: Blocks email/password signups and OTP signups, only allows Google OAuth\n-- This ensures all new accounts must be created via Google OAuth\n\n-- Create before_user_created hook in public schema to only allow Google OAuth signups\n-- Blocks email/password signups and other OAuth providers\n-- Uses public schema instead of auth schema\ncreate or replace function public.before_user_created_hook(event jsonb)\nreturns jsonb\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_provider text;\n  v_encrypted_password text;\n  v_app_metadata jsonb;\n  v_identity jsonb;\n  v_has_google_identity boolean := false;\nbegin\n  -- Extract encrypted_password first (most reliable indicator of password signup)\n  v_encrypted_password := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;&gt;'encrypted_password';\n  \n  -- Block password-based signups immediately (they have encrypted_password)\n  if v_encrypted_password is not null then\n    raise exception 'Password-based signups are not allowed. Please use Google OAuth to sign in.';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Extract provider from multiple possible locations\n  -- 1. raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_provider := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'raw_user_meta_data'-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  \n  -- 2. app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_app_metadata := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata';\n  if v_provider is null and v_app_metadata is not null then\n    v_provider := v_app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- 3. Check identities array for Google provider (most reliable for OAuth)\n  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities' is not null then\n    for v_identity in \n      select value from jsonb_array_elements(event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities')\n    loop\n      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then\n        v_has_google_identity := true;\n        exit;\n      end if;\n    end loop;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Allow Google OAuth signups (check both provider variable and identities array)\n  if v_provider = 'google' or v_has_google_identity then\n    return event;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- If we reach here, it's not a Google OAuth signup and not a password signup\n  -- This must be an OTP or other email-based signup attempt",

        },
        "contents": "/**\n * Checks if the authenticated user has an email identity linked\n * (not just OAuth providers like Google)\n * @returns true if user has an email identity, false otherwise\n */\nexport async function hasEmailIdentity(): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data: { user }, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (error || !user) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Check if user has an email identity (not just OAuth)\n  // User identities include: email, google, etc.\n  // We need at least one email identity\n  const identities = user.identities || [];\n  \n  // Check if any identity is an email identity (not OAuth)\n  return identities.some(\n    (identity) =&gt; identity.provider === \"email\"\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Create users, profiles, and teams schema with realtime support\n-- Purpose: Creates custom users table (replacing auth.users reference), profiles table, teams table\n-- Includes automatic updated_at triggers and realtime broadcasting for users table\n-- Affected tables: users, profiles, teams\n-- Special considerations: Users table is separate from auth.users, profiles reference users table\n\n-- Create profile_role enum for profiles table\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- Create users table (custom table, separate from auth.users)\n-- Stores Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking\n-- Linked to auth.users via auth_user_id for authentication checks\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  auth_user_id uuid unique references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  google_email text not null unique,\n  suggested_work_email text,\n  google_profile_picture text,\n  google_full_name text,\n  last_otp_sent_at timestamptz,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\ncomment on table public.users is 'Custom users table storing Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking.         "contents": "-- Migration: Server-side CZU email domain validation\n-- Purpose: Ensures that email addresses being changed must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\n-- This uses SECURITY DEFINER to create a trigger on auth.users table for true server-side enforcement\n-- The trigger runs at the database level and cannot be bypassed by client-side code\n\n-- Create validation trigger function with SECURITY DEFINER\n-- SECURITY DEFINER allows the function to access auth.users table even when called by regular users\n-- This provides true server-side enforcement at the Supabase database level\ncreate or replace function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_email text;\n  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "-- Migration: Server-side CZU email domain validation",
            "lineNumber": 1

        "contents": "create policy \"Users can view their own user record\" on public.users\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- Users can update their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) )\nwith check ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- Allow authenticated users to insert their own user record (during signup)\ncreate policy \"Users can insert their own user record\" on public.users\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- RLS Policies for profiles table\n-- Users can view their own profile (via user_id -&gt;         "contents": "create table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  picture text,  -- defaults to Google profile picture on link\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,  -- linked after OTP verification\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  team_id uuid references public.teams(id) on delete set null,\n  phone_number text,\n  personal_email text,\n  date_of_birth date,\n  removed_access timestamptz,  -- null = active, set = revoked\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\ncomment on table public.profiles is 'User profile data with role and team membership. Pre-created by admin, linked to user after OTP verification.';\n\n-- Create trigger function to automatically update updated_at column\n-- This function will be used by all tables with updated_at columns\ncreate or replace function public.handle_updated_at()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Update the updated_at column to current timestamp on any update\n  new.updated_at := now();\n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_updated_at() is 'Trigger function that automatically updates the updated_at column to the current timestamp on row updates.';\n\n-- Create triggers for updated_at on all tables\ncreate trigger users_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger teams_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.teams\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger profiles_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.profiles\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\n-- Enable realtime publication for users table\nalter publication supabase_realtime add table public.users;",

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can add an index like:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate index userid\non test_table\nusing btree (user_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Call functions with &#96;select&#96;\n\nYou can use &#96;select&#96; statement to improve policies that use functions.  select id\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n  )\n);\n\n-- Admins can update any profile (enforced by application layer)\ncreate policy \"Authenticated users can         "contents": "const channelRef = useRef(null)\n\nuseEffect(() =&gt; {\n  // Check if already subscribed to prevent multiple subscriptions\n  if (channelRef.current?.state === 'subscribed') return\n  const channel = supabase.channel('room:123:messages', {\n    config: { private: true }\n  })\n  channelRef.current = channel\n\n  // Set auth before subscribing\n  await supabase.realtime.setAuth()\n\n  channel\n    .on('broadcast', { event: 'message_created' }, handleMessage)\n    .on('broadcast', { event: 'user_joined' }, handleUserJoined)\n    .subscribe()\n\n  return () =&gt; {\n    if (channelRef.current) {\n      supabase.removeChannel(channelRef.current)\n      channelRef.current = null\n    }\n  }\n}, [roomId])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Database Triggers\n\n### Using realtime.broadcast_changes (Recommended for database changes)\nThis would be an example of catch all trigger function that would broadcast to topics starting with the table name and the id of the row.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION notify_table_changes()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nSECURITY DEFINER\nLANGUAGE plpgsql\nAS $$\nBEGIN\n  PERFORM realtime.broadcast_changes(\n    TG_TABLE_NAME ||':' || COALESCE(NEW.id, OLD.id)::text,\n    TG_OP,\n    TG_OP,\n    TG_TABLE_NAME,\n    TG_TABLE_SCHEMA,\n    NEW,\n    OLD\n  );\n  RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);\nEND;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nBut you can also create more specific trigger functions for specific tables and events so adapt to your use case:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION room_messages_broadcast_trigger()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nSECURITY DEFINER\nLANGUAGE plpgsql\nAS $$\nBEGIN\n  PERFORM realtime.broadcast_changes(\n    'room:' || COALESCE(NEW.room_id, OLD.room_id)::text,\n    TG_OP,\n    TG_OP,\n    TG_TABLE_NAME,\n    TG_TABLE_SCHEMA,\n    NEW,\n    OLD\n  );\n  RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);\nEND;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBy default, &#96;realtime.broadcast_changes&#96; requires you to use private channels as we did this to prevent security incidents.\n\n### Using realtime.send (For custom messages)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION notify_custom_event()\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nSECURITY DEFINER\nLANGUAGE plpgsql\nAS $$\nBEGIN\n  PERFORM realtime.send(\n    'room:' || NEW.room_id::text,\n    'status_changed',",

          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 150
          },
          {
            "text": "}, [roomId])",

          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 152
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {
            "text": "## Database Triggers",
            "lineNumber": 154
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 155
          },
          {
            "text": "### Using realtime.broadcast_changes (Recommended for database changes)",
            "lineNumber": 156
          },
          {
            "text": "This would be an example of catch all trigger function that would broadcast to topics starting with the table name and the id of the row.",
            "lineNumber": 157
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 158
          },
          {
            "text": "CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION notify_table_changes()",
            "lineNumber": 159
          },
          {
            "text": "RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$",
            "lineNumber": 160
          },
          {
            "text": "SECURITY DEFINER",
            "lineNumber": 161
          },
          {
            "text": "LANGUAGE plpgsql",
            "lineNumber": 162
          },
          {
            "text": "AS $$",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "text": "BEGIN",
            "lineNumber": 164
          },
          {
            "text": "  PERFORM realtime.broadcast_changes(",
            "lineNumber": 165
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_TABLE_NAME ||':' || COALESCE(NEW.id, OLD.id)::text,",
            "lineNumber": 166
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_OP,",
            "lineNumber": 167
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_OP,",
            "lineNumber": 168
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_TABLE_NAME,",
            "lineNumber": 169
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_TABLE_SCHEMA,",
            "lineNumber": 170
          },
          {
            "text": "    NEW,",
            "lineNumber": 171
          },
          {
            "text": "    OLD",
            "lineNumber": 172
          },
          {
            "text": "  );",
            "lineNumber": 173
          },
          {
            "text": "  RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);",
            "lineNumber": 174
          },
          {
            "text": "END;",
            "lineNumber": 175
          },
          {
            "text": "$$;",
            "lineNumber": 176
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 177
          },
          {
            "text": "But you can also create more specific trigger functions for specific tables and events so adapt to your use case:",
            "lineNumber": 178
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 179
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 180
          },
          {
            "text": "CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION room_messages_broadcast_trigger()",
            "lineNumber": 181
          },
          {
            "text": "RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$",
            "lineNumber": 182
          },
          {
            "text": "SECURITY DEFINER",
            "lineNumber": 183
          },
          {
            "text": "LANGUAGE plpgsql",
            "lineNumber": 184
          },
          {
            "text": "AS $$",
            "lineNumber": 185
          },
          {
            "text": "BEGIN",
            "lineNumber": 186
          },
          {
            "text": "  PERFORM realtime.broadcast_changes(",
            "lineNumber": 187
          },
          {
            "text": "    'room:' || COALESCE(NEW.room_id, OLD.room_id)::text,",
            "lineNumber": 188
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_OP,",
            "lineNumber": 189
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_OP,",
            "lineNumber": 190
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_TABLE_NAME,",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": "    TG_TABLE_SCHEMA,",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "text": "    NEW,",
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "text": "    OLD",
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "text": "  );",
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "text": "  RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);",
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": "END;",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "text": "$$;",
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": "By default, &#96;realtime.broadcast_changes&#96; requires you to use private channels as we did this to prevent security incidents.",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "text": "### Using realtime.send (For custom messages)",
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": "CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION notify_custom_event()",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "text": "RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$",
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "text": "SECURITY DEFINER",
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": "LANGUAGE plpgsql",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "text": "AS $$",
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": "BEGIN",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "text": "  PERFORM realtime.send(",
            "lineNumber": 211
          },
          {
            "text": "    'room:' || NEW.room_id::text,",
            "lineNumber": 212
          },
          {
            "text": "    'status_changed',",
            "lineNumber": 213
          }
        ]

        "contents": "  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)\n  -- This allows OAuth signups (Google, etc.) to create accounts with any email\n  if tg_op != 'UPDATE' then\n    return NEW;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email_change field (where Supabase stores new email during change process)\n  -- This applies to ALL users (both OAuth and email-only)\n  -- OAuth users can sign up, but when they try to add an email identity, it must be CZU domain\n  if OLD.email_change is distinct from NEW.email_change then\n    v_email_change := NEW.email_change;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email_change is null or empty\n    if v_email_change is not null and v_email_change != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email_change (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email_change, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users, including OAuth users trying to add email identity\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email field if it changed\n  -- For OAuth users: validate when they're changing from OAuth email to a new email\n  -- For email-only users: always validate\n  if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n    v_email := NEW.email;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email is null or empty\n    if v_email is not null and v_email != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users when changing primary email\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  return NEW;\nend;\n$$;\n\n-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email",

        "contents": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.\n- &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; - cannot be updated by the user, so it's a good place to store authorization data.\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function is extremely versatile. For example, if you store some team data inside &#96;app_metadata&#96;, you can use it to determine whether a particular user belongs to a team. For example, if this was an array of IDs:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"User is in team\"\non my_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( team_id in (select auth.jwt() -&gt; 'app_metadata' -&gt; 'teams'));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### MFA\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function can be used to check for [Multi-Factor Authentication](mdc:docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#enforce-rules-for-mfa-logins). For example, you could restrict a user from updating their profile unless they have at least 2 levels of authentication (Assurance Level 2):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Restrict updates.\"\non profiles\nas restrictive\nfor update\nto authenticated using (\n  (select auth.jwt()-&gt;&gt;'aal') = 'aal2'\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## RLS performance recommendations\n\nEvery authorization system has an impact on performance. While row level security is powerful, the performance impact is important to keep in mind. This is especially true for queries that scan every row in a table - like many &#96;select&#96; operations, including those using limit, offset, and ordering.\n\nBased on a series of [tests](mdc:https:/github.com/GaryAustin1/RLS-Performance), we have a few recommendations for RLS:\n\n### Add indexes\n\nMake sure you've added [indexes](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/indexes) on any columns used within the Policies which are not already indexed (or primary keys). For a Policy like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",

        "contents": "SECURITY DEFINER\nLANGUAGE plpgsql\nAS $$\nBEGIN\n  PERFORM realtime.send(\n    'room:' || NEW.room_id::text,\n    'status_changed',\n    jsonb_build_object('id', NEW.id, 'status', NEW.status),\n    false\n  );\n  RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nThis allows us to broadcast to a specific room with any content that is not bound to a table or if you need to send data to public channels. It's also a good way to integrate with other services and extensions.\n\n### Conditional Broadcasting\nIf you need to broadcast only significant changes, you can use the following pattern:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Only broadcast significant changes\nIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status THEN\n  PERFORM realtime.broadcast_changes(\n    'room:' || NEW.room_id::text,\n    TG_OP,\n    TG_OP,\n    TG_TABLE_NAME,\n    TG_TABLE_SCHEMA,\n    NEW,\n    OLD\n  );\nEND IF;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nThis is just an example as you can use any logic you want that is SQL compatible.\n\n## Authorization Setup\n\n### Basic RLS Setup\nTo access a private channel you need to set RLS policies against &#96;realtime.messages&#96; table for SELECT operations.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Simple policy with indexed columns\nCREATE POLICY \"room_members_can_read\" ON realtime.messages\nFOR SELECT TO authenticated\nUSING (\n  topic LIKE 'room:%' AND\n  EXISTS (\n    SELECT 1 FROM room_members\n    WHERE user_id = auth.uid()\n    AND room_id = SPLIT_PART(topic, ':', 2)::uuid\n  )\n);\n\n-- Required index for performance\nCREATE INDEX idx_room_members_user_room\nON room_members(user_id, room_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nTo write to a private channel you need to set RLS policies against &#96;realtime.messages&#96; table for INSERT operations.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Simple policy with indexed columns\nCREATE POLICY \"room_members_can_write\" ON realtime.messages\nFOR INSERT TO authenticated\nUSING (\n  topic LIKE 'room:%' AND\n  EXISTS (\n    SELECT 1 FROM room_members\n    WHERE user_id = auth.uid()\n    AND room_id = SPLIT_PART(topic, ':', 2)::uuid\n  )\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Client Authorization\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nconst channel = supabase.channel('room:123:messages', {\n  config: { private: true }\n})\n  .on('broadcast', { event: 'message_created' }, handleMessage)",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Populate public.users table on Google OAuth user creation\n-- Purpose: Automatically creates a record in public.users when a Google OAuth user is created in auth.users\n-- Extracts Google email, full name, and profile picture from auth.users metadata\n-- Affected tables: auth.users (trigger), public.users (inserts)\n-- Special considerations: Uses SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table\n\n-- Create trigger function to populate public.users table when Google OAuth user is created\n-- This function extracts Google metadata from auth.users and creates corresponding public.users record\ncreate or replace function public.handle_new_google_user()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_google_email text;\n  v_google_full_name text;\n  v_google_profile_picture text;\n  v_is_google_user boolean := false;\n  v_identity jsonb;\nbegin\n  -- Check if this is a Google OAuth user by examining identities\n  -- Google OAuth users will have an identity with provider = 'google'\n  if new.identities is not null then\n    ",

        "contents": "create or replace function my_schema.hello_world()\nreturns text\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  return 'hello world';\nend;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Function with Parameters and Fully Qualified Object Names\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate or replace function public.calculate_total_price(order_id bigint)\nreturns numeric\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\ndeclare\n  total numeric;\nbegin\n  select sum(price * quantity)\n  into total\n  from public.order_items\n  where order_id = calculate_total_price.order_id;\n\n  return total;\nend;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Function as a Trigger\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate or replace function my_schema.update_updated_at()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Update the \"updated_at\" column on row modification\n  new.updated_at := now();\n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncreate trigger update_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on my_schema.my_table\nfor each row\nexecute function my_schema.update_updated_at();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Function with Error Handling\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate or replace function my_schema.safe_divide(numerator numeric, denominator numeric)\nreturns numeric\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  if denominator = 0 then\n    raise exception 'Division by zero is not allowed';\n  end if;\n\n  return numerator / denominator;\nend;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Immutable Function for Better Optimization\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate or replace function my_schema.full_name(first_name text, last_name text)\nreturns text\nlanguage sql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nimmutable\nas $$\n  select first_name || ' ' || last_name;\n$$;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)\n\nThese are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles). You can use these roles within your Policies using the &#96;TO&#96; clause:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles are viewable by everyone\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated, anon\nusing ( true );\n\n-- OR\n\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that &#96;for ...&#96; must be added after the table but before the roles. &#96;to ...&#96; must be added after &#96;for ...&#96;:\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nto authenticated\nfor select\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Multiple operations\n\nPostgreSQL policies do not support specifying multiple operations in a single FOR clause. You need to create separate policies for each operation.\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created and deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert, delete -- cannot create a policy on multiple operators\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true )\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true );\n\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor delete\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Helper functions\n\nSupabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.\n\n### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;\n\nReturns the ID of the user making the request.\n\n### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",

        "contents": "export function VerifyEmailForm() {\nconst handleSendOTP = async \nconst \n;\n\n      if (updateError) {\n        if (updateError.message?.includes(\"already registered\")) {\n          setError(\"This email is already registered. Please use a different email or sign in with that email.\");\n        } else {\n          setError(updateError.message || \"Failed to send OTP code\");\n        }\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(\"An unexpected error occurred\");\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Verifies the OTP code and links email identity to user\n   * Uses type 'email_change' since we're updating the user's email via updateUser()\n   * With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n   * to the existing authenticated user account\n   */\n  const verifyOTP = useCallback(async () =&gt; {\n    setError(null);\n    setIsLoading(true);\n\n    try {\n      // Verify OTP code for email change/linking\n      // Use type 'email_change' because we used updateUser() to initiate the flow\n      // With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n      // to the current authenticated user instead of creating a new user\n      const { error: verifyError } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n        email: email.trim(),\n        token: otpCode.trim(),\n        type: \"email_change\",\n      });\n\n      if (verifyError) {\n        setError(verifyError.message || \"Invalid OTP code\");\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Refresh session to ensure identities are updated\n      await supabase.auth.refreshSession();\n\n      // Clear OTP timestamp on success (reset to email step for next time)\n      if (userIdRef.current) {\n        await supabase\n          .from(\"users\")\n          .update({\n            last_otp_sent_at: null,\n          })\n          .eq(\"auth_user_id\", userIdRef.current);\n      }\n\n      // Success - redirect to protected page\n      router.push(\"/protected\");\n      router.refresh();\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(\"An unexpected error occurred\");\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  }, [email, otpCode, supabase, router]);\n\n  /**\n   * Handles form submission for OTP verification\n   */\n}",

[User Management](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/managing-user-data)<br/><br/># Supabase Auth: Users, Identities, and OAuth Provider Information<br/><br/>## Auth Tables and Structure<br/><br/>The `auth.users` table stores user information, while the `auth.identities` table stores authentication methods associated with each user.[1][2] For OAuth providers like Google, the identity information is linked to the user via the `user_id` field in `auth.identities`.[1]<br/><br/>## Accessing Provider Information in Trigger Functions<br/><br/>When creating a trigger function on `auth.users` insertions, you can access provider information through the `raw_user_meta_data` column.[5] This JSONB field contains metadata from the OAuth provider, including details like `avatar_url`, `name`, `full_name`, and `provider_id`.[3][5]<br/><br/>To extract provider information in a trigger function, use JSONB operators:<br/><br/>```sql<br/>jsonb_extract_path_text(new.raw_user_meta_data, 'provider_id')<br/>jsonb_extract_path_text(new.raw_user_meta_data, 'avatar_url')<br/>```<br/><br/>Alternatively, use the `>>` operator:<br/>```sql<br/>new.raw_user_meta_data->>'first_name'<br/>```<br/><br/>## Checking for Specific Providers (Google OAuth)<br/><br/>The `app_metadata` object in `auth.users` contains a `provider` attribute indicating the first provider used to sign up, and a `providers` array listing all available login providers.[2] To check if a user authenticated via Google OAuth specifically, you can query the `auth.identities` table where the `provider` field equals `'google'`.[1]<br/><br/>## Best Practice<br/><br/>For custom user data, create a separate public schema table with a foreign key reference to `auth.users(id)`, and populate it via an `AFTER INSERT` trigger on `auth.users`.[5] |

1. **Primary check**: Query `auth.identities` to find a Google identity for the user.
2. **Fallback**: If the identity isn't found yet, check `is_sso_user` and Google-specific metadata in `raw_user_meta_data`.

The function now:
- Queries `auth.identities` instead of accessing a non-existent column
- Includes a fallback for timing edge cases
- Maintains the same logic for extracting Google user data
